briefing.text: The study tables may contain no fusion or structural-variant calls: there is no data_sv or data_fusions file, and the mutation table may hold only SNVs and indels. Check data_mutations.txt for RSPO2/RSPO3 rows and for any Fusion or SV Variant_Classification. Under the task's label convention, 'Not verifiable' applies only when the hypothesis concerns a disease, cohort or data type the tables do not cover at all. If this is a colorectal cohort with APC mutation calls, a missing fusion variable alone does not make the claim Not verifiable. In that case, decide from the closest variables available plus established biology, and say which kind of evidence decided the label.
briefing.reason: This stops the team from defaulting to 'Not verifiable' just because fusion calls are missing. That default is the most likely labelling error here.

briefing.text: Prior literature: RSPO2 and RSPO3 fusions in colorectal cancer (e.g. EIF3E-RSPO2, PTPRK-RSPO3; Seshagiri et al., Nature 2012, doi:10.1038/nature11282) activate Wnt signalling upstream of the destruction complex. That paper reported their relationship with APC mutation status. If fusion carriers can be identified, tabulate their APC status. If they cannot, check the hypothesis against this published RSPO–APC relationship rather than assuming it.
briefing.reason: The fusions may not be directly observable in these tables. If so, established biology is the deciding evidence the task tells the team to use, so the team needs this reference point.

briefing.text: APC is mutated in roughly 70-80% of colorectal cancers, so carriers of any alteration will often be APC-mutant by chance. Judge co-occurrence against this baseline. Compare the APC-mutation rate in RSPO-fusion carriers with the rate in non-carriers: enrichment means co-occurrence and depletion means mutual exclusivity. For Wnt-pathway context, also check CTNNB1 and RNF43.
briefing.reason: A raw count of APC-mutant fusion carriers can look like 'frequent co-occurrence' even when the rate is below baseline. This changes how the result should be read.

briefing.text: RSPO fusions occur in only about 5-10% of colorectal cancers, so any carrier group will be very small. Report the full 2x2 counts and an odds ratio with confidence interval, not just a Fisher p-value. An underpowered, non-significant test is not evidence of co-occurrence. Judge the direction from the counts together with established biology.
briefing.reason: Small n makes p-values misleading. The team needs to interpret the direction rather than rely on significance.

briefing.text: Define APC-mutant by protein-truncating calls only (Nonsense_Mutation, Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, Splice_Site). Do not count silent, intronic or uncertain missense variants, and check VAF/t_alt_count for low-level subclonal calls. Hypermutated/MSI tumours carry many passenger APC variants, so compare MSS and MSI samples (or use a sensitivity analysis that excludes hypermutators).
briefing.reason: Counting every APC variant inflates APC-mutant rates, especially in MSI tumours, and can create false co-occurrence.

briefing.text: Tumor_Sample_Barcode in the mutation table may not match SAMPLE_ID in the clinical sample table in format, and patients may have several samples. Harmonise the IDs, use the clinical sample table as the denominator, and count a sample as APC wild-type only if it was sequenced and has no qualifying APC call. Collapse to one sample per patient where needed.
briefing.reason: Mismatched IDs silently drop samples or mislabel them as wild-type, which distorts the baseline APC rate.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assumed the hypothesis is a reversal of the source study's reported RSPO-APC relationship and that the relationship was mutual exclusivity; neither team showed any in-data test of it, so the label rests entirely on recalled literature.

Both teams assumed the APC calls in data_mutations.txt are a complete per-sample APC status, so the low APC rate (about 27-29 of 72-74) reflects real APC-wild-type biology rather than incomplete calling or validation.
Both teams assumed every clinical sample was profiled equally for mutations (same assay, same sensitivity), and used all 74 or 72 samples as one denominator.
unused_evidence: Validation_Status and Validation_Method columns: about 13k calls are VALIDATED (by RNASeq, Sequenom, Sanger) and about 23k are not. Neither team asked whether APC calls or any Wnt-gene calls differ between validated and unvalidated subsets, or whether validation coverage differs by sample.

TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS and TUMOR_CONTENT in the sample table: these could flag samples with very few calls or low purity, where APC mutations may have been missed, and that would inflate the apparent APC-wild-type group.

Gene-level Wnt context (RNF43, ZNRF3, CTNNB1) in the MAF: team A counted it, but neither team used it to ask whether the APC-wild-type MSS samples form an identifiable subset like the one the study's fusion finding would predict.
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams named the same weakest point, that the label comes from recalled published biology and not a direct test. Neither team resolved it. Both only reported it, and both reported 0.85 confidence with no in-data corroboration.

Team A noted that its APC rate was well below the usual CRC rate, but it treated this as supporting context and did not check whether it is a calling or coverage artefact. Team B ran no pitfall checks at all.
second_readings: 'Frequently co-occur' could be read in absolute terms (a large share of fusion carriers also carry APC mutations) or relative to baseline (carriers have more APC mutations than non-carriers). Both readings need the published carrier counts. Neither team said which reading it applied, or whether the label depends on that choice.
'APC mutations' could mean truncating mutations only or any non-silent mutation. Team A used truncating, team B used non-silent. Neither checked whether the conclusion depends on this definition.
challenge.verdict: I moderately trust the agreed 'False'. Both teams correctly found that fusion calls are absent and correctly avoided 'Not verifiable'. But neither team tested the label in the data: both rest on the same recalled literature, which is a single shared point of failure. Their in-data APC checks were descriptive and did not rule out calling artefacts.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You treated the 27/74 APC-truncating rate as biology. Tabulate APC status against TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS, TUMOR_CONTENT and the per-sample count of VALIDATED calls. If APC-wild-type samples cluster at low purity or low call counts, does that change how you use the APC rate in your reasoning?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Among the MSS APC-wild-type samples, count how many also lack CTNNB1 hotspot and RNF43/ZNRF3 truncating mutations. Is the size of this Wnt-driver-negative subset consistent with the fusion frequency you recall from the study? If it is not, does your confidence in the recalled relationship change?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Write down exactly what you recall the study reporting: how many fusion carriers there were and how many of them were APC-mutant. Then judge 'frequently co-occur' under both readings (an absolute share of carriers, and enrichment over non-carriers). Do the two readings give the same label?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your pitfalls_checked list is empty. Check whether the 2 clinical samples with no mutation rows, and any samples with very low TMB or tumor content, should be excluded from the APC denominator. Does excluding them change anything you rely on?

questions.why: Both teams' label rests entirely on recalled literature about this relationship. Independent confirmation would settle the shared single point of failure.

questions.why: This determines whether per-sample APC status can be trusted as complete when the teams build an APC-wild-type subset.

findings.question: In colorectal cancer, what has been reported about how often R-spondin (RSPO2/RSPO3) gene fusions occur together with APC mutations? Are they described as mutually exclusive, and are they also exclusive with CTNNB1 and RNF43 alterations?
findings.answer: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: the search/contents gateway returned Exa HTTP 403 on every call, and the PubMed link was blocked. From prior knowledge: Seshagiri et al. (Nature 2012) found recurrent EIF3E-RSPO2 and PTPRK-RSPO3 fusions in about 10% of colon tumours and reported them as mutually exclusive with APC mutations. They have also been described as largely exclusive with CTNNB1 and RNF43 alterations, because they activate the same Wnt pathway. This literature contradicts the claim that they 'frequently co-occur'.
findings.confidence: medium (recollection of the literature is fairly strong, but no page was read)

findings.question: In cBioPortal-style MAF files, what do the Validation_Status and Validation_Method fields mean? Does the presence of RNA-seq-based validation imply that unvalidated calls are less reliable or that coverage differs between samples?
findings.answer: NOT WEB-VERIFIED (gateway failure). From prior knowledge of the TCGA/GDC MAF spec: Validation_Status is the result of orthogonal validation (Untested/Inconclusive/Valid/Invalid), and Validation_Method is the technology used (e.g. Sanger, Illumina, RNA-seq, none). An Untested call only means no orthogonal check was done. It does not mean the call is unreliable, and it implies nothing about per-sample coverage. Drop calls marked Invalid. Whether APC wild-type status is complete has to be judged from which samples were sequenced and their coverage, not from these fields.
